summary: Request: RSS/API feed for model updates + changelog entries (machine-readable)
description:
Customer request (Northpeak Research):
- They want a machine-readable feed of model updates (new models, new model versions, deprecations) to integrate into their internal change-management + evaluation pipeline.
- Preferred formats:
  1) RSS/Atom feed for humans/ops notifications
  2) API/JSON endpoint for automation
- They also asked if responses can include the resolved model version, so they can correlate behavior changes to release notes.

Impact:
- Not an outage, but blocks their ability to automate monitoring and review of changes. They cited prior incidents with other providers where model behavior changed without a clear announcement.

Current state (as of ticket):
- We do not have a GA RSS/API feed for model changelog yet.
- Some customers rely on ad-hoc announcements and/or manual review of docs pages.

What Support communicated:
- We confirmed this is in active development as part of the “customer-visible model changelog” project.
- We will provide:
  - Customer-visible model changelog entries (per model + per version)
  - An RSS/Atom feed option (docs)
  - A public JSON feed / API endpoint for automation
  - API/SDK surfaces to expose resolved model_version + changelog_url

Requested next steps from customer:
- Clarify: do they need per-model feeds only, or a global feed across all models?
- Clarify: do they want only published entries (customer-safe) or also draft/pre-release notes? (We expect published only.)

Internal tracking:
- Logged as product feedback; linked to PM taxonomy definition (PM-801) and generator/publish work (ENG-4926) + API surfacing (ENG-4928).

Workaround offered:
- Until the feed is available, Support can provide a periodic summary of model changes upon request, and we can proactively notify them for deprecations impacting models they use (manual process).

Notes:
- Customer specifically requested that entries be immutable/auditable once published (append-only or superseding corrections), and that the API provide stable identifiers for entries so they can ingest and dedupe reliably.
